patch_resolves_note: The fixed PowerPC asm-writer reroutes `TBEGIN` to operand slot 0, so the same `printU1ImmOperand()` helper now executes with an in-range operand index and the subsequent `printUInt32()` sink consumes a fully initialized 32-bit immediate instead of stale `mci` stack bytes from slot 1.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the PowerPC instruction word that drives the vulnerable `TBEGIN` decode and print path.

Root cause. The generated PowerPC asm-writer encodes the `TBEGIN` printer metadata as `820308`, and fragment-0 bits `(820308 >> 14) & 31 == 18` route `PPC_TBEGIN` into case 18, which prints operand slot 1. The fix changes this entry to `263252`, whose fragment-0 bits select case 16 so `TBEGIN` prints operand 0 instead.
MemorySanitizer crash site. The uninitialized value loaded from `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal` reaches `printUInt32()` as `val` and is consumed by this branch.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `u1imm_operand_load.loaded_value_bits == print_uint32_sink.val_bits`.
